record.original_question: Does there exist a notion of duality for codes over non-Abelian groups that yields a MacWilliams formula, and if so is there at least some subclass of non-Abelian groups for which such a duality and MacWilliams formula can be made to work?

evidence.quote: Open Question 4.3. Is there a duality and MacWilliams formula for codes over non-Abelian groups? Is there a subclass of non-Abelian groups for which a duality and a MacWilliams formula exists?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $n \geq 1$. A (group) code of length $n$ over $G$ is a subgroup $C \leq G^n$. When $G$ is abelian, the classical MacWilliams identity relates the complete weight enumerator of $C$ to that of its dual code $C^\perp \leq \widehat{G}^n$ (where $\widehat{G}$ is the Pontryagin dual), via the character table of $G$.

Question: Does there exist a notion of duality $C \mapsto C^\perp$ for codes $C \leq G^n$ over non-abelian finite groups $G$ that produces a MacWilliams-type identity, i.e., a linear transformation expressing a suitable weight enumerator of $C^\perp$ in terms of that of $C$ (and vice versa) so that the enumerators of $C$ and $C^\perp$ determine each other? If no such duality exists for all non-abelian finite groups, identify a non-trivial subclass of non-abelian finite groups for which such a duality together with a MacWilliams identity can be defined.
artifact.status_search_result: There are both negative and positive results. A negative result establishes that no traditional duality theory on all subgroups of $G^n$ can satisfy a MacWilliams identity for any non-abelian $G$. However, recent work has proposed alternative notions of duality for non-abelian group codes that do yield MacWilliams-type identities (and Greene-type theorems), reducing to the classical formulas when $G$ is abelian. Thus the original question is partially answered: pure subgroup duality fails, but modified frameworks succeed.

status_evidence.title: No MacWilliams duality for codes over nonabelian groups
status_evidence.snippet: Shows there does not exist a nonabelian group G with a duality theory on subgroups of G^n for all n satisfying MacWilliams.
status_evidence.claim: Negative result: standard subgroup duality fails for non-abelian groups.

status_evidence.title: A duality for nonabelian group codes
status_evidence.snippet: Defines a notion of duality generalizing the abelian case and proves Greene's theorem and MacWilliams identities for nonabelian group codes.
status_evidence.claim: A modified duality with MacWilliams identity exists for non-abelian group codes.

status_evidence.title: On a duality for codes over non-abelian groups
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates dualities for codes over non-abelian groups in Designs, Codes and Cryptography.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work refines the duality framework for non-abelian group codes.
